mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that dampens corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the unemployment rate signals a tightening monetary policy during a strong labor market, which typically leads to a contraction in corporate profit margins and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS up and UNRATE down) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE is declining in a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past three months indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with rising consumer confidence and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 for two consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 115.0 for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annually), a surge in retail sales (RSAFS) above the 90th percentile of its 12-month distribution signals strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS is above the 90th percentile in a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a rapidly tightening labor market that boosts wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.
